scholarships.title: Joint Japan/World Bank Graduate Scholarship Program (JJ/WBGSP) 2027 - Application Window for Japanese Nationals
scholarships.official_source: World Bank, Development Economics Vice Presidency, JJ/WBGSP Secretariat (scholarship fully funded by the Government of Japan)

existing.description: This is the Japanese-nationals track of the Joint Japan/World Bank Graduate Scholarship Program, which the World Bank states is fully funded by the Government of Japan. It funds up to two years for a limited number of Japanese mid-career professionals dedicated to the alleviation of poverty and enhanced shared prosperity in developing countries who have been admitted to or are currently enrolled in a master's or PhD programme outside Japan in a development-related field. Benefits include one economy class air travel to the host university and a $600 travel allowance at the start, one economy class return travel and a $600 travel allowance at the end, tuition, basic medical insurance obtainable through the university, and a monthly subsistence allowance to cover all living expenses while on campus. The amount of the monthly subsistence allowance varies by host country and is not published on the page.
eligibility: On or after the date the call for scholarship applications opens, not be an Executive Director, his/her alternate, and/or staff of any type of appointment (including temporary and consultant) of the World Bank Group (The World Bank, International Development Association, International Finance Corporation, Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency, and International Center for Settlements of Investment Disputes), and not be a close relative of any of the aforementioned by blood or adoption (close relative defined as Mother, Father, Sister, Half-sister, Brother, Half-brother, Son, Daughter, Aunt, Uncle, Niece, or Nephew)
Hold a bachelor's degree (or equivalent university degree) earned at least three years before the date of the Application Deadline

On or after the date the JJ/WBGSP scholarship application process opens, not be employed (as a staff or any type of employment) by the Government of Japan or its related agencies, including JICA, local governments and the Central Bank

Have at least 3 years of paid development-related employment acquired since earning a bachelor's degree (or equivalent university degree) and acquired within the past six years from the date of the Application Deadline

At the time of the application submission, be either admitted unconditionally (except for financing) or currently enrolled full-time in a graduate program outside of Japan in an area of study related to development, or be currently employed full-time in development-related work pertaining directly to developing countries
existing.eligibility_summary: Be a Japanese national; hold a bachelor's degree (or equivalent) earned at least three years before the Application Deadline; have at least 3 years of paid development-related employment acquired within the past six years from the deadline; and be admitted unconditionally except for financing to, or currently enrolled full-time in, a development-related graduate programme outside Japan.
benefits: The scholarship is fully funded by the Government of Japan
All JJ/WBGSP scholarships cover the duration of the graduate program or two years, whichever is less
Two separate $600 travel allowances are payable, one at the start of the programme and one at the end
coverage: One economy class air travel from the scholar's home country to the host university at the start of the graduate degree program, if the scholar is not already attending the graduate program, plus a $600 travel allowance

One economy class air travel from the host university to Japan or to a developing country where the scholar has secured employment at the end of the scholarship period, if the scholar has completed all requirements to earn the graduate degree, plus a $600 travel allowance
Tuition for the graduate program for the duration of the scholarship period
Cost of basic medical insurance that can be obtained through the university

Monthly subsistence allowance to cover all living expenses while on campus during the scholarship period, including accommodations, food and books; the amount varies depending on the host country and is not published
requirements: Register interest with the JJ/WBGSP Secretariat by emailing scholarshipapplicants@worldbank.org from February 15, 2027
Details on eligibility criteria for each call for applications are provided in that call's Application Guidelines, and those detailed criteria are strictly adhered to with no exceptions

Be admitted unconditionally (except for financing) to, or currently enrolled full-time in, a graduate program outside of Japan in an area of study related to development, or be currently employed full-time in development-related work pertaining directly to developing countries
Inform and document to the JJ/WBGSP Secretariat any other sources of scholarship funds if notified of being a semi-finalist or awarded a scholarship
application_method: From February 15, 2027, express interest to the JJ/WBGSP Secretariat by emailing scholarshipapplicants@worldbank.org
Be admitted unconditionally (except for financing) to, or already be enrolled full-time in, a development-related master's or PhD programme outside Japan
Gather the documents required by the 2027 Application Guidelines for Japanese Nationals
Submit the application within the window closing April 16, 2027
Await the JJ/WBGSC decision; winners are informed by mid-July
existing.selection_notes: Two qualified assessors independently review each eligible application and score it on a scale of 1 to 10 on four factors: Quality of Academic Experience and Recommendation (20% weight), Quality of Professional Recommendations (20% weight), Quality of Professional Experience (20%), and Commitment to International Development Career (40% weight). The Secretariat uses the average score of the two assessors plus maintaining a reasonable distribution of awards across gender and giving scholarships to those applicants who, other things being equal, have limited access to financial resources for graduate studies abroad. Finalists are presented to the JJ/WBG Steering Committee, composed of members of the World Bank Board of Directors and World Bank management, for approval.
existing.best_fit: Japanese nationals with a bachelor's degree earned at least three years before the deadline and at least three years of paid development-related employment acquired within the past six years, who are admitted unconditionally (except financing) to, or already enrolled full-time in, a development-related master's or PhD programme outside Japan.
existing.notes: The scholarship does NOT cover visa application costs, expenses to bring and/or support family members, extra-curricular courses or training, courses below the minimum credits required for the degree, language training not provided by the graduate program, additional travel during the study program, research or supplementary educational materials, field trips, workshops, seminars or internships, educational equipment such as computers, and the resident permit fee. The scholarship may only supplement, and does not duplicate, any other source of financial support; if you are notified of being a semi-finalist or are awarded, you must inform and document other scholarship funds to the Secretariat. After earning their degree, Japanese national scholars are expected to advance their professional career with a keen focus on the alleviation of poverty and enhanced shared prosperity in developing countries. The air travel benefit at the end of the scholarship period is conditional on having completed all requirements to earn the graduate degree, and the return ticket is to Japan or to a developing country where the scholar has secured employment. The published US$600 is a per-trip travel allowance, not the award total. The 2026 window for Japanese nationals closed on Friday 17 April 2026, so only the 2027 window is live.
existing.duration: Up to two years; all JJ/WBGSP scholarships cover the duration of the graduate program or two years, whichever is less
existing.application_period: A single application window for the 2027 cycle for Japanese nationals, from February 15 to April 16, 2027. From the opening date, prospective candidates are invited to register interest with the Secretariat by email. Results are communicated by mid-July 2027.
existing.deadline_display: The 2027 application window for Japanese nationals will open from February 15 to April 16, 2027. As from February 15, 2027, prospective candidates are invited to express their interest to the JJ/WBGSP Secretariat with an email to scholarshipapplicants@worldbank.org. Winners are informed by mid-July, after the JJ/WBGSC approval. The 2026 application window for Japanese nationals closed on Friday 17 April 2026.
existing.program_type: Development bank scholarship (bilateral government-funded graduate scholarship)

scholarships.title: Kyushu University Friendship Scholarship
scholarships.degree: Undergraduate, Master's, PhD (exchange, special auditing, special research or double degree enrolment at Kyushu University)

existing.description: Kyushu University's own support programme for privately financed international students who come to Kyushu University on exchange, special auditing, special research or double degree status and who cannot afford to study in Japan solely at their own expense. It pays a monthly stipend of JPY 80,000, and the total of all scholarships held by the grantee may not exceed that amount. Applicants apply through their prospective host department at Kyushu University, not directly to the university centre. There are two recruitment periods per fiscal year: Period I around February for students who will study from April to September, and Period II around May for students who will study from October to March. The period of stay must be 3 months, 5 months (one semester) or 11 months (two semesters).
eligibility: Currently a student at an overseas university

Host status at Kyushu University is one of: special auditing student or special research student under an inter-university exchange agreement; special auditing student or special research student under an inter-departmental exchange agreement; double degree programme student under a double degree agreement; or special auditing student or special research student from a university with no student exchange agreement
Acceptance in Japan must begin within the academic year, for a stay of 3 months, 5 months (1 semester) or 11 months (2 semesters)
Unable to study in Japan solely at their own expense because of financial reasons
Certain to obtain Student status of residence while studying at Kyushu University

Must return to the home university after completing their studies at Kyushu University to obtain a degree or graduate; students scheduled to withdraw or be expelled, and those who complete a regular course of study at Kyushu University, are not eligible

Excellent academic records and character, with a grade evaluation coefficient of 2.30 or higher on a 3-point scale for the previous year, calculated by the method specified by the Japan Student Services Organization
existing.eligibility_summary: Non-Japanese nationals who are students at an overseas university and whose status at Kyushu University is as a special auditing student, special research student or double degree programme student under an inter-university exchange agreement, an inter-departmental exchange agreement, a double degree agreement, or even from a university with no exchange agreement. They must begin their stay within the academic year for 3, 5 or 11 months, be unable to study in Japan solely at their own expense, be certain to obtain Student status of residence, return to their home university afterwards to obtain a degree or graduate, and have excellent academic records and character with a grade evaluation coefficient of 2.30 or higher on a 3-point scale for the previous year.
benefits: Support for special auditing students, special research students and double degree programme students, who have few other scholarship opportunities
Available to students from universities with no student exchange agreement with Kyushu University
Under some Kyushu University descriptions, waiver of examination, matriculation and tuition fees according to the relevant exchange agreement
coverage: Cap: the total of this and any other scholarships held may not exceed JPY 80,000 per month
Period of stay of 3 months, 5 months or 11 months
requirements: Applications are made through the prospective host department at Kyushu University, not to the International Student Support Center
The period of stay must be 3 months, 5 months or 11 months and must begin within the academic year
The grantee must return to the home university to obtain a degree or graduate; those who complete a regular course of study at Kyushu University are not eligible
The combined total of all scholarships held by the grantee may not exceed JPY 80,000 per month
A grade evaluation coefficient of 2.30 or higher on a 3-point scale for the previous year is required, calculated by the JASSO method
documents: Application made through the prospective host department at Kyushu University
Acceptance or eligibility for the relevant exchange, special auditing, special research or double degree status at Kyushu University
Evidence of financial difficulty in studying in Japan
Proof of Student status of residence eligibility
Academic records showing a grade evaluation coefficient of 2.30 or higher on a 3-point scale for the previous year
Confirmation from the home university that the student will return to complete their degree
Any further documents requested by the host department
existing.english_requirement: No English test requirement is published for this scholarship. The admission or exchange route and any language requirements come from the specific host department and the exchange agreement under which the student will study at Kyushu University.
application_method: Identify the department at Kyushu University that would host you and contact the person in charge of the exchange programme, or the faculty or graduate school student affairs office
Confirm the application method and eligibility requirements with that department
Apply for the scholarship through the host department during the relevant recruitment period
Period I (around February) is for study starting April to September; Period II (around May) is for study starting October to March
Await the department's selection and the university's decision
existing.selection_notes: Kyushu University describes the scheme as an invitation to students from abroad who attend prestigious universities in their home country and who will play an important role in their nation's future, aiming to foster future leaders, maintain good relations with Kyushu University and act as a point of contact for joint research. Selection is carried out through the host department, and eligibility criteria are the eight main requirements published by the International Student Support Center.
existing.best_fit: Students at overseas universities, including universities without an exchange agreement with Kyushu University, who are coming to Kyushu University as special auditing or special research students or on a double degree programme and cannot fund the stay themselves.
existing.notes: Kyushu University publishes two different descriptions of a scholarship with this name. The International Student Support Center page gives a JPY 80,000 monthly cap and stays of 3, 5 or 11 months. A Graduate School of Engineering page describes a Kyushu University Friendship Scholarship of JPY 80,000 per month for undergraduates and JPY 100,000 for graduate students, travel expenses of up to JPY 100,000, terms of 3 to 12 months and up to 8 students per term, with examination, matriculation and tuition fees waived according to the relevant exchange agreement. Confirm the applicable variant with the host department before applying.
existing.duration: 3 months, 5 months (one semester) or 11 months (two semesters) at Kyushu University; the period of stay must begin within the academic year
existing.application_period: Two recruitment periods a year. Period I: around February, for study starting between April and September. Period II: around May, for study starting between October and the following March.
existing.deadline_display: No exact date is published. There are two recruitment periods in each fiscal year: Period I is recruited around February for grantees starting between April and September, and Period II is recruited around May for grantees starting between October and March. Applications are made through the applicant's prospective host department at Kyushu University, so the department sets its own internal date within the period.
existing.program_type: University exchange scholarship (Kyushu University's own scheme)
